{
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "issue_category", "analytical_usefulness": 0.55, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "rationale": "A cause/type axis useful for grouping, but largely redundant with the existing original 'category' column, dampening its analytical leverage. Values (connectivity, database, email) are soundly read from short_description."},
    {"name": "scope_of_impact", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Scope (individual vs department vs infrastructure-wide) is a strong new axis plausibly linked to resolution time. Department/individual readings are supported by text (e.g. 'sales department'), but 'infrastructure_wide' being the top value (312) is not obviously warranted for many terse descriptions, so some inference is aggressive."},
    {"name": "failure_mechanism", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Mechanism is a genuinely useful causal axis for the query. However, values like 'connection_refused' for 'VPN connection issue' or 'Cannot connect to database' assert a specific failure mode the text does not state; 'server_unresponsive' for 'Email system not working properly' is likewise an invented specific. Frequent unsupported specificity lowers groundedness."},
    {"name": "environment_specificity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Environment (production/on-premise/remote_vpn) is a useful control/grouping axis. 'remote_vpn' for VPN and 'office_on_premise' for department WiFi are supported, but 'production' for 'Cannot connect to database' is an inference beyond the text; mostly reasonable with occasional overreach."},
    {"name": "problem_specificity", "analytical_usefulness": 0.7, "source_groundedness": 0.8, "rationale": "Distinguishing well-defined vs vague/broad descriptions is a legitimate axis that could correlate with resolution time. Judgments (e.g. 'vague_or_generic' for 'Email system not working properly') are reasonable readings of the description text."},
    {"name": "recurring_pattern", "analytical_usefulness": 0.35, "source_groundedness": 0.25, "rationale": "A recurrence flag would be useful in principle, but nothing in a single short_description supports whether an issue recurs; every sampled row is labelled 'True' with no cross-row evidence provided. This is a confident specific the source cannot ground, and near-constant (360/140) skews it toward low leverage."},
    {"name": "assignment_stability", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Whether the same person opened/closed the incident is a plausible driver of resolution time and is derivable from original assigned_to/closed_by fields. Well grounded, though it is derived from existing columns rather than the text."},
    {"name": "incident_closure_status", "analytical_usefulness": 0.2, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "A boolean closed/not-closed flag is trivially redundant with the existing 'state'/'closed_at' columns and adds little new analytical leverage for explaining resolution-time drivers. Values are derivable from closed_at."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.62,
  "source_groundedness": 0.68,
  "rationale": "Several added columns (scope_of_impact, failure_mechanism, environment_specificity, problem_specificity, assignment_stability) provide genuine new causal/grouping axes well aligned with the query about drivers of resolution time. Weaknesses: issue_category duplicates the original category; incident_closure_status duplicates state/closed_at; recurring_pattern is both near-unsupported by single-row text and near-constant. Groundedness is generally acceptable for categorisations read from short_description, but failure_mechanism and some scope/environment values assert specific mechanisms the terse text does not state, indicating over-confident inference in places."
}
